sections.html:
Two Buffalo offices handle the tax side of owning here. The Assessor puts a value on each parcel. The Collector sends statements and receives payment from the Dallas County Administration Building, 102 S Cedar Street, Buffalo, MO 65622 (mail to PO Box 529). Phone (417) 345-7836 on non-holiday weekdays, 8:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:00.

Call the Assessor at (417) 345-8774 (PO Box 263) about the assessed value of real or personal property, a changed name or address, a vehicle listed by mistake or a legal description. Bring a statement that never came, or a question about how collection works, to the Collector. Other county lines: Clerk (417) 345-2632, Recorder (417) 345-2242, Treasurer (417) 345-2020.

November is when real estate and personal property statements go out. Pay whenever yours arrives, but after December 31 it is delinquent. If November ends and you have no statement, ring the Collector at once.

  • For checks in the mail, the postmark has to read December 31 or sooner.
  • A later postmark gets the check sent back, unless penalty and interest are added.
  • Unpaid prior years come first, and the office will not take the current year until they are cleared.
  • Enclose the bottom stub of the statement when mailing. One check may pay several bills.

You can pay in person, by mail or at dallascountymocollector.com with cash, personal check, money order, cashier's check, or a debit or credit card, though cards bring a convenience fee. Paying tax on someone else's parcel, or missing one of your own, is not the Collector's responsibility, so read the legal description on each statement.

sections.h2: How a Dallas County house is valued
sections.html:
State rules sort real estate into classes with different assessment rates: 19% of market value for residential property, 12% of production value for agricultural land and 32% for everything else. The county has 541 square miles of land and had about 31.6 residents per square mile in 2020.

The levies of the school, fire and other districts apply to the assessed figure, and the Assessor can tell you which levies fit your parcel. With just thirteen permits issued in 2025, resale houses make up nearly everything buyers see.

sections.h2: If you think your assessment is too high
sections.html:
Begin by calling the Assessor to ask how your number was reached. Still unhappy? RSMo 137.275 lets you take it to the county board of equalization by the second Monday in July, appearing yourself, sending an attorney or agent, or writing a letter. For hearing dates, ring the County Clerk at (417) 345-2632.

RSMo 138.060 has the board hear appeals summarily, giving the assessor's figure no head start. When a parcel's assessed valuation jumped by 15% or more over the last assessment, and not because of new construction or improvements, the burden of proof moves to the assessor. Hold on to your increase notice, and gather photographs, repair estimates or recent sales of similar homes to show the value is too high. Paper evidence beats a phone call.

The State Tax Commission is the next level, available under RSMo 138.430 inside the chapter's time limit or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later. It corrects assessments it finds unlawful, unfair, improper, arbitrary or capricious. Disputes over exemption or the wrong taxing location belong in circuit court, filed within 30 days.

Delinquent parcels go on the auction block every year on August's fourth Monday, 10:00 a.m., at the Dallas County Annex Building in Buffalo. RSMo 140.150 puts the next sale in August 2027. Until a parcel actually sells, you can still pay the taxes, penalty, interest and costs.

  • A bidder must live in Missouri or appoint an agent who does.
  • The sale notice warns that a parcel may carry hazardous waste, liens or condemned buildings.
  • The owner has a year after the sale to redeem.
  • Bid money above the tax amount earns no interest.

The Collector has to mail the recorded owner a first class notice before parcels are advertised, and a certified notice too when assessed value is over $1,000. Missing the letter does not wipe out the tax. If you are behind, ask the Assessor which mailing address is on file.

sections.h2: Other Collector services for new owners
sections.html:
Beyond tax bills, the Collector's desk also handles utility taxes, merchant and auctioneer license fees and duplicate receipt fees, and writes tax exempt waivers where they apply.

A person arriving from another state has 30 days to obtain Missouri plates and a Missouri driver's license. The Collector's site lists what plates require: title or registration, proof of insurance, a Missouri inspection certificate, and either a validated tax receipt from the Collector or a non-assessment clearance from the Assessor. Someone coming from another Missouri county should request an assessment sheet from the Assessor before March 1 to avoid a penalty. Your own buyer may be a newcomer like this, so pass these steps along.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Dallas County
sections.html:
Buffalo is both the seat and the largest city, and the county is part of the Springfield metro area.

Gather a few things before listing: the latest statement for each parcel, the legal description from the deed, and the Collector's current payoff. If you own personal property such as a vehicle in the county, tax on it follows its own cycle, so settle that account separately from the land. Closing goes faster when the tax record is clean, because a buyer's lender will want to see it, and the title company can order the figures for you.

When your house sells, have the title company request a current statement from the Collector and settle the year's tax at the table. If the transfer comes after the November mailing, let the Collector know where the new bill should go. Back taxes on a parcel have to be paid before the office takes the current year, so a house with several unpaid years needs the whole stack cleared before closing. Ask the Collector for each year's balance separately, then add them up with the title company before you set a closing date. That way no unpaid year surprises you at the table. Cash Home Buyers can buy a house in that position and let the closing agent pay the Collector from the price.

faqs.q: When does Dallas County tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Once December 31 passes. A statement can be paid on receipt, and mailed checks need a postmark of that day or sooner. Anything later is returned without penalty and interest. If November ends with no statement, phone (417) 345-7836.

faqs.q: What are the Collector's office hours and address?
faqs.a: Find it in the Dallas County Administration Building at 102 S Cedar Street, Buffalo, MO 65622. It opens weekdays 8:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:00, and mail goes to PO Box 529.
That is the Assessor, (417) 345-8774. Since the Collector bills from the Assessor's records, take value, owner name, vehicle and legal description questions there.

faqs.q: What date ends the window to appeal to the board of equalization?
faqs.a: RSMo 137.275 sets it at the second Monday in July. You can attend, send an attorney or agent, or submit a letter, and the County Clerk can give you the hearing schedule.

faqs.q: When is the delinquent land sale?
faqs.a: Every year on the fourth Monday of August, and the next is in August 2027. Owners may pay before the sale and then have a year to redeem.
